summary: Parallax Fire turns NASA's two fire-detection records into one honest record of when a place burns. MODIS (Terra and Aqua, since 2000) sees fires in 1 km pixels; VIIRS (since 2012) sees 375 m pixels and records about five times more detections in Bangladesh, so the joined record makes burning seem to jump in 2012, when mostly the camera changed. We harmonized the two: an XGBoost model learns how MODIS and VIIRS relate only from years when both flew (2013–2020), and we tested it on 2023–2024, years it never saw. In Bangladesh it missed by 98 detections a month, against 627 for the raw MODIS count; California also passed, while New South Wales did not, so there the app shows the raw records only and says so. The free web app gives planners, researchers and teachers a 25-year burning calendar, district maps, a one-switch "one scale" view and a live 3D Earth with the five fire satellites and today's NASA FIRMS hot spots. Every estimate is labelled, and missing data is never shown as zero.
details:
THE CHALLENGE

NASA has watched fires from space for more than 20 years, but with two different cameras. MODIS (Terra and Aqua, since 2000) sees the ground in 1 km pixels. VIIRS (Suomi NPP from 2012, then NOAA-20 and NOAA-21) sees 375 m pixels and catches smaller fires: in Bangladesh it records about five times as many detections. Join the two records and burning seems to leap in 2012. A planner comparing 2005 with 2020 could ask for help against a change that never happened on the ground.

HOW IT WORKS

1. Data: NASA FIRMS yearly country archives (MODIS C6.1 2001–2025, VIIRS S-NPP 375 m 2012–2025) for Bangladesh, the USA and Australia, counted per 5 km cell and month.

2. Learning: an XGBoost model learns how the two records relate, only from years when both satellites flew (trained 2013–2020, method chosen on 2021–2022), and gives a likely range (8 in 10).

3. Checking: 2023–2024 were held back. Average miss per month: Bangladesh 98 (raw MODIS count 627, simple monthly rule 109); California 794 (2,219; 909). New South Wales was closer than both rules (375 vs 4,087 and 1,640), but its likely range was too wide, so the app shows the raw records only there and says so.

4. A real test: March 2024 in Bangladesh. VIIRS counted 621, MODIS 111. From MODIS alone we estimated about 1,093, likely 571–1,529; the real 621 fell inside.

WHAT YOU CAN DO

- Calendar: 25 years by month for Bangladesh and its divisions, California and New South Wales.

- Two satellites: one switch shows the records joined or on one scale.

- Map: 5 km squares or Bangladesh districts on a real basemap.

- Story: March 2024, step by step.

- Live: a 3D Earth lit by the real Sun, the five fire satellites at their real positions, and the last 24 hours of NASA FIRMS hot spots, counted per satellite; NASA GIBS imagery on the map.

- Results and Data & sources: every number traced to its file, with downloads and a PDF manual.

WHO IT HELPS

District and forest planners who need the real burning season, researchers comparing decades without mistaking a new camera for new fire, and teachers showing why data needs care.

TOOLS

- Data and model: Python (pandas, NumPy, XGBoost, scikit-learn, PyTorch, Shapely) in two Kaggle notebooks (download and verify NASA FIRMS archives; train, test and export).

- App: TypeScript, React, Vite, three.js, GSAP, MapLibre GL JS, satellite.js (SGP4 orbits); hosted on Netlify, with small serverless functions for the live NASA feeds; installable and works offline for the archive.

- Checks: Vitest unit tests and Playwright browser checks; checksums for every data file.

- Code: https://github.com/Shahriar290900/Harmonisation-MODIS-VIIRS

CREATIVITY

"Parallax": the same fire seen by two cameras looks different. Instead of hiding that, the app makes it visible: one switch, a step-by-step real example, and a live Earth showing the actual satellites next to what they detected today.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

Honesty (estimates labelled, gaps shown as gaps, a hot spot is not a confirmed wildfire, per-region results, no forecasting claims); plain language for non-experts; phones and low bandwidth (heavy training ran on Kaggle, and the app caches the archive offline).

WHAT'S NEXT

More regions and districts; following NOAA-20 and NOAA-21 as the Suomi NPP data stream ends; a Bangla interface; and testing with the people who plan for burning seasons.
